TF-IDF represents documents numerically by considering the importance of terms within a document collection.
Precision and recall are evaluation metrics commonly used for classification models.
A classification model predicts a discrete label from one or more input features.

Data normalization transforms numerical values into a comparable scale.
Tokenization is the process of breaking text into smaller units such as words or tokens.
Stop words are common words that may be removed during some text preprocessing workflows.

Recall measures the proportion of actual positive cases that a classification model successfully identifies.

TF IDF assigns higher importance to terms that are frequent in one document but less common across the collection.
A confusion matrix compares predicted class labels with the actual class labels.

Feature scaling transforms numerical features so that they operate on comparable scales.
Logistic regression can be used for classification by estimating the probability of class membership.
A pipeline combines multiple machine learning preprocessing and modeling steps into one workflow.

Model accuracy represents the proportion of predictions that match the actual labels.
